355.title: The Circle Spinout Nobody Googles
355.text: OpenTrade was spun out from Circle, which is why its vault contracts run on Circle's own open-source Perimeter Protocol — an origin that lends credibility and implies institutional DNA without requiring Circle's blessing. XMMF holds Fidelity's USD Money Market Fund through a Cayman SPC with J.P. Morgan as both custodian and broker, which is institutional plumbing worthy of a product ten times its $39 million size. Avalanche hosts roughly three-quarters of supply, an unusual distribution for an EVM-native product, explained by early partnerships with Avalanche-native institutional DeFi integrations. With no CoinGecko listing and no DefiLlama stablecoin coverage, XMMF exists almost entirely within the authenticated OpenTrade dashboard and a handful of Avalanche protocols — the tokenized equivalent of a well-run operation that has no particular interest in being discovered.

usdt-tether.title: Too Big to Depeg
usdt-tether.text: The 800-pound gorilla of stablecoins commands more market cap than most countries' GDP and settles more volume daily than Visa. Despite years of "where are the reserves?" discourse, Tether keeps printing — and keeps getting redeemed at par. Its BDO Italia attestations have quieted skeptics somewhat, but the real moat is simpler: when every exchange, DeFi protocol, and OTC desk denominates in USDT, switching costs approach infinity. Love it or hate it, the market has voted with its liquidity.

usdc-circle.title: The Regulated Runner-Up
usdc-circle.text: Circle's USDC is what happens when you build a stablecoin for compliance officers. Full monthly attestations from Deloitte, SEC registration, and a BlackRock-managed reserve fund make it the institutional darling of the space. The March 2023 SVB depeg briefly shattered its reputation for safety — and its market cap still hasn't fully recovered to pre-crisis levels. For anyone who needs a stablecoin their legal team won't flinch at, USDC remains the default.

dai-makerdao.title: The OG Decentralized Dollar
dai-makerdao.text: The stablecoin that proved crypto could create a synthetic dollar without a bank account. DAI survived the March 2020 crash, navigated the USDC depeg contagion, and maintained its peg through sheer overcollateralization. Now overshadowed by its own rebrand (USDS) and increasingly backed by RWAs rather than pure crypto collateral, DAI remains the philosophical North Star that most "decentralized" stablecoins claim to be inspired by.

frax-frax.title: The Identity Crisis
frax-frax.text: Frax started life as crypto's boldest algorithmic experiment -- a fractional-reserve stablecoin that actually worked. Then it quietly abandoned the algorithm, went 100% USDC-collateralized, and launched frxUSD backed by BlackRock's BUIDL fund. The original FRAX is now labeled "Legacy Frax Dollar" with a shrinking supply, while frxUSD chases institutional credibility. It's a remarkable pivot from "trust the math" to "trust BlackRock," and the market cap of both combined still barely registers against USDC.

tusd-trueusd.title: The Fallen Faithful
tusd-trueusd.text: Once positioned as the transparent alternative to Tether, TrueUSD has fallen from grace with a market cap that's a fraction of its peak. Regulatory issues, questions about its Prime Trust relationship, and a depeg incident in 2023 eroded the trust its name once implied. It persists more as a cautionary tale about counterparty risk than as a competitive stablecoin.

lusd-liquity.title: Decentralization's Last Stand
lusd-liquity.text: LUSD is one of the few stablecoins that can genuinely claim decentralization -- immutable contracts, ETH-only collateral, no governance keys, no admin functions. The trade-off is a modest market cap that makes it a rounding error in the stablecoin landscape. Liquity V2 launched BOLD as the successor with user-set interest rates and multi-collateral support. LUSD remains the philosophical benchmark against which every "decentralized" stablecoin should be measured, even as the market has clearly decided it prefers convenience over purity.

mim-abracadabra.title: Scandal-Proof Somehow
mim-abracadabra.text: Multiple hacks, a founder whose Wonderland treasury manager turned out to be a convicted fraudster from the QuadrigaCX collapse, and a governance token down 99% from its all-time high -- yet MIM still trades near peg. Abracadabra's model of lending against yield-bearing collateral remains clever in theory, but the protocol's security record reads like a cautionary tale for smart contract auditors. At this point, holding MIM requires less trust in the math and more faith in Daniele Sestagalli's ability to keep rebuilding after each crisis.

usdp-paxos.title: The Quiet Regulator's Pet
usdp-paxos.text: Paxos's original stablecoin is the definition of doing everything right and getting ignored for it. NYDFS-regulated since 2018, KPMG-audited, reserves in bankruptcy-remote accounts, monthly attestations -- and a market cap that barely moves the needle. Paxos's real business is issuing stablecoins for others (PayPal's PYUSD, formerly Binance's BUSD). USDP is less a product and more a proof of concept that Paxos can be trusted with your brand.

usdd-tron-dao-reserve.title: Justin Sun's Undying Dollar
usdd-tron-dao-reserve.text: USDD 2.0 emerged from its rocky algorithmic era with crypto collateral and a fresh governance model, though the centralized-dependent tag tells you Justin Sun still has the keys. It persistently trades above peg, which sounds good until you realize the premium reflects illiquidity as much as demand. The TRON ecosystem keeps it alive; whether that's a feature or a risk depends on your priors about its founder.

dola-inverse-finance.title: The Comeback CDP
dola-inverse-finance.text: Inverse Finance lost $24M across two oracle manipulation exploits in 2022, accumulating bad debt that would have buried most protocols. Instead, the DAO spent years clawing its way back -- selling tokens to investors, building the FiRM fixed-rate lending protocol, and launching a PSM backed by Sky's sUSDS. The sDOLA yield-bearing wrapper earning organic lending revenue is the kind of unsexy, sustainable DeFi that rarely makes headlines but actually works.

gusd-gemini.title: The Ghost Dollar
gusd-gemini.text: Gemini Dollar was one of the first NYDFS-regulated stablecoins, launched in 2018 with the Winklevoss seal of approval and State Street Bank custody. Years later it has a minimal market cap, near-zero DeFi presence, and exchange delistings that keep shrinking its already thin liquidity. Without aggressive exchange partnerships, GUSD is a museum piece: historically significant, technically sound, and gathering dust.

alusd-alchemix.title: Time Pays Your Debt
alusd-alchemix.text: Alchemix's self-repaying loans remain one of DeFi's most elegant ideas: deposit stablecoins, borrow up to 50%, and let yield gradually erase your debt. No liquidations, no interest payments -- just the slow passage of time converting future yield into present liquidity. The V3 upgrade nearly doubled capital efficiency, but the governance token trades at a fraction of its peak. alUSD is a stablecoin for patient DeFi users who've read the docs, which may explain why the broader market hasn't noticed.

susd-synthetix.title: The Longest Depeg
susd-synthetix.text: Synthetix's sUSD spent much of 2025 below peg after SIP-420 slashed the collateralization ratio from 750% to 200% and forgave staker debt. The structural incentive for stakers to buy discounted sUSD to repay their own debt -- the reflexive mechanism that maintained the peg for years -- was simply removed. Recovery plans involving exchange-fee buybacks and basis-trade vaults may work, but sUSD is now a case study in how upgrading peg mechanics mid-flight can go sideways.

ousd-origin-protocol.title: The Passive Yield Play
ousd-origin-protocol.text: Origin Dollar is the stablecoin that pays you to hold it -- no staking, no locking, just a rebasing balance that grows as the protocol deploys USDC into Morpho and Curve strategies. The clever twist is that smart contracts must explicitly opt in to receive yield, so OUSD held in non-opted AMM pools effectively subsidizes everyone else's returns. It's a well-engineered product for the small cohort of users who want DeFi yield without the DeFi homework.

cusd-celo.title: The Mobile-First Dollar
cusd-celo.text: Celo Dollar is what happens when you build a stablecoin around phone numbers instead of wallet addresses. The Mento reserve backing it holds USDC, DAI, BTC, ETH, and CELO at a reported 393% overcollateralization ratio -- impressive until you remember that a crypto-heavy reserve can evaporate fast in a downturn. Celo's migration to an Ethereum L2 gives cUSD access to a broader ecosystem, and validators like Google Cloud and Deutsche Telekom lend institutional credibility. With its current market cap, cUSD remains a niche stablecoin for emerging-market payments rather than a DeFi building block.

eurc-circle.title: The Euro's Best On-Chain Bet
eurc-circle.text: Circle's euro stablecoin brings the same reserve transparency and regulatory posture as USDC to the eurozone. MiCA-compliant and fully backed, EURC is positioning itself as the default EUR stablecoin before regulations force weaker competitors out. The euro stablecoin market is nascent enough that first-mover advantage still matters — and Circle is determined to be the name that sticks.

eurs-stasis.title: MiCA's Biggest Winner
eurs-stasis.text: Stasis Euro went from afterthought to contender largely because MiCA regulation cleared the field and EURS was already compliant. Malta-based, BDO-audited, and holding an EMI license since 2022, EURS was positioned for exactly this regulatory moment. The irony is that its explosive growth happened not because the product changed, but because competitors got disqualified. The looming threat is a consortium of European banks planning their own MiCA-compliant euro stablecoin, which would bring the kind of distribution that Stasis cannot match.

ceur-celo.title: The Other Mento Euro
ceur-celo.text: Celo Euro shares the same Mento reserve and algorithmic stability mechanism as cUSD, just pegged to the euro instead. With a small market cap and trading volumes that barely register outside of Celo-native DEXs, cEUR exists primarily to serve Celo's vision of region-specific stablecoins for mobile payments. The 393% overcollateralization ratio provides a generous buffer, but the crypto-heavy reserve composition means cEUR's stability in a severe downturn remains untested at any meaningful scale.

eura-angle.title: Angle's DeFi Euro
eura-angle.text: Angle Protocol's EURA is one of the few crypto-backed euro stablecoins — an overcollateralized design in a market dominated by RWA-backed issuers. Its centralized-dependent governance means community involvement with practical guardrails. For DeFi purists who want a euro without bank dependencies, EURA is one of the few options on the menu.

fpi-frax.title: Frax's Inflation Hedge
fpi-frax.text: Frax Price Index is pegged not to a currency but to the CPI — a stablecoin that tries to preserve purchasing power rather than nominal value. It's algorithmic, experimental, and philosophically interesting: why peg to a dollar that loses value annually when you can peg to the cost of living? The execution challenges of maintaining a CPI peg are considerable, but the concept alone makes FPI the most intellectually honest "stable" coin in the market.

uusd-youves.title: Tezos's Quiet Giant
uusd-youves.text: Youves' uUSD commands a dominant share of Tezos DeFi TVL, making it the largest protocol on a chain most people have forgotten about. The 300% overcollateralization in XTZ provides a generous safety margin. The catch is near-zero trading volume on major aggregators, reflecting the reality that uUSD is deeply liquid within its own ecosystem and essentially invisible outside it. It's a functioning, well-designed CDP stablecoin stranded on an island that the broader crypto market stopped visiting.

lisusd-lista.title: BNB Chain's CDP Bet
lisusd-lista.text: Lista DAO's lisUSD borrows MakerDAO's CDP playbook and transplants it to BNB Chain, where Binance's gravitational pull does the marketing. Collateral includes BNB, ETH, and liquid staking tokens, with a PSM accepting USDT, USDC, and FDUSD for peg stability. The plan to transition from MakerDAO's codebase to Liquity's is ambitious, and whether lisUSD can grow beyond Binance-subsidized adoption remains the central question.

euroe-membrane.title: Paxos's EU Passport
euroe-membrane.text: EUROe started as a Finnish EMI-regulated euro stablecoin from Membrane Finance, KPMG-audited and quietly competent. Then Paxos acquired Membrane Finance specifically to gain MiCA compliance across 30 European countries -- making EUROe less a standalone product and more Paxos's entry ticket to the EU market. Its future depends entirely on whether Paxos decides to scale EUROe as-is or rebrand it into its broader institutional stablecoin platform alongside USDP, PYUSD, and USDG.

eure-monerium.title: Monerium's Electronic Money
eure-monerium.text: Monerium's EURe is one of the few stablecoins licensed as electronic money in the EEA, meaning it's legally equivalent to a bank balance. It connects directly to IBAN accounts, making fiat on/off-ramps seamless in a way most stablecoins only promise. Its small scale belies its regulatory significance: EURe is what euro stablecoins look like when they actually comply with European financial law.

eusd-electronic-usd.title: The Yield Mirage
eusd-electronic-usd.text: Lybra Finance promised high APY just for holding eUSD, funded by ETH liquid staking yields flowing through to stablecoin holders. The protocol peaked at $400M TVL in 2023, then collapsed as yields compressed and attention moved elsewhere. eUSD now trades below peg with near-zero social activity, and the protocol offers USDC redemptions for eUSD holders -- the clearest possible signal of a wind-down. A cautionary tale about building a stablecoin around a yield narrative that couldn't survive a single market cycle.

crvusd-curve.title: Curve's Own Medicine
crvusd-curve.text: When the protocol that handles more stablecoin volume than anyone else launches its own stablecoin, the design better be interesting -- and crvUSD delivers. The LLAMMA mechanism replaces hard liquidations with gradual, continuous rebalancing through price bands, letting collateral be automatically rebought if prices recover. The Peg Stability Reserve maintains the dollar peg through four PegKeeper pools paired with USDC, USDT, PYUSD, and frxUSD -- each a centralized dependency that the crypto-native collateral was supposed to avoid. The savings vault (scrvUSD) creates a self-correcting feedback loop where depeg pressure increases yields, attracting buyers back. It's technically sophisticated, but a stablecoin whose peg mechanism lives or dies by four centralized counterparties has traded one risk for four others.

gho-aave.title: Aave's Dollar
gho-aave.text: GHO is what happens when the largest lending protocol decides to mint its own stablecoin. Borrowers on Aave can mint GHO at favorable rates, creating a dollar tightly coupled to Aave's ecosystem health. The peg has been stable since the rocky first months, and stkAAVE discounts give governance participants a reason to borrow. It's DeFi-native in a way that few stablecoins genuinely are.

fdusd-first-digital.title: Binance's Current Favorite
fdusd-first-digital.text: First Digital USD rose to prominence as Binance's preferred stablecoin after BUSD's regulatory demise. Hong Kong-based and reserve-backed, it serves as the default trading pair on the world's largest exchange. Its fate is tied to Binance's continued endorsement — a single point of dependency that the market has apparently accepted.

pyusd-paypal.title: Big Fintech's Entry Ticket
pyusd-paypal.text: PayPal's stablecoin proves that when a payments giant with 400 million users issues a dollar token, people notice. Paxos-issued and fully reserved in treasuries and cash, PYUSD's regulatory credentials are impeccable. Its challenge isn't trust — it's utility. Until DeFi and PayPal's walled garden meaningfully converge, it risks being the best-credentialed stablecoin nobody uses on-chain.

gyen-gyen.title: The Yen's Only Option
gyen-gyen.text: GYEN is the world's first and essentially only regulated JPY-pegged stablecoin, issued by GMO Trust under a NYDFS trust charter with reserves at FDIC-insured banks. The market for a yen stablecoin is inherently niche -- Japan's own regulatory framework for stablecoins remains restrictive, and the JPY's persistent weakness against the dollar limits demand from non-Japanese users. GYEN's value proposition is less about competing with dollar stablecoins and more about being the only credible digital yen when someone finally needs one.

usdy-ondo-finance.title: Ondo's Yield Machine
usdy-ondo-finance.text: Ondo Finance's USDY offers tokenized US Treasury exposure to everyone outside the US, neatly sidestepping domestic securities law. It's RWA-backed, yield-bearing, and has become the poster child of the "tokenized treasuries" narrative. The irony of a product that democratizes US government debt by excluding US persons is apparently lost on no one.

cadc-cad-coin.title: Canada's Lonely Loonie
cadc-cad-coin.text: CADC is a 1:1 Canadian dollar stablecoin from PayTrie, backed by reserves at a tier-1 Canadian bank and registered with FINTRAC as a money services business. It's now on Ethereum, Polygon, Arbitrum, Base, and Solana. The Canadian stablecoin market is wide open -- the Bank of Canada has urged federal regulation -- and CADC's bet is that being the first compliant CAD stablecoin matters more than being the biggest.

usde-ethena.title: The Basis Trade, Tokenized
usde-ethena.text: Ethena's USDe pioneered the delta-neutral stablecoin: hold spot crypto, short the perps, pocket the funding rate. It works beautifully in bull markets when longs pay shorts handsomely for leverage. The catch? When funding flips negative — as it inevitably does — the insurance fund becomes the only thing between USDe and a death spiral. It's a sophisticated yield product wearing a stablecoin's clothing.

aeur-anchored-coins.title: The Swiss Euro
aeur-anchored-coins.text: Anchored Coins' AEUR offers a Swiss-regulated, reserve-backed euro stablecoin that targets the intersection of European money and Swiss financial infrastructure. Its smaller market cap belies a clean regulatory setup. In the euro stablecoin race, AEUR competes on jurisdiction prestige rather than distribution scale.

buck-bucket-protocol.title: Sui's CDP Experiment
buck-bucket-protocol.text: Bucket Protocol brings the MakerDAO playbook to the Sui ecosystem: deposit SUI, BTC, ETH, or LSTs, mint a dollar stablecoin at zero interest, get liquidated at 110% collateral ratio. The PSM module accepts USDC and USDT for peg stability, which is a polite way of saying the decentralized stablecoin ultimately leans on centralized ones when it matters. It's a competent CDP implementation searching for scale on a chain still searching for DeFi depth.

vchf-vnx.title: The Swiss Franc, Tokenized
vchf-vnx.text: VNX's VCHF is one of the first licensed Swiss franc stablecoins, issued out of Liechtenstein under FMA licenses. At modest market cap and daily volume measured in tens of thousands, VCHF is less a liquid trading instrument and more a proof-of-concept that CHF can exist on-chain. For the small audience that specifically needs a regulated Swiss franc token, it's one of the only games in town.

veur-vnx.title: Liechtenstein's Quiet Euro
veur-vnx.text: VNX Euro shares its sibling VCHF's regulatory pedigree under Liechtenstein's FMA. At thin liquidity, VEUR is dwarfed by Circle's EURC and the MiCA-compliant competition. Its multi-chain availability across Ethereum, Polygon, Avalanche, and Solana is a nice touch for a token that very few people are currently moving.

audd-novatti.title: Australia's Dollar On-Chain
audd-novatti.text: AUDD is one of those rare stablecoins that actually makes geographic sense: an Australian dollar token from an ASX-listed parent company (Novatti), audited by William Buck, and regulated under ASIC/AFSL. More interesting is its selection for the Reserve Bank of Australia's Project Acacia, testing tokenized asset settlement. Whether Australia's stablecoin market can sustain a domestic alternative to USD-denominated tokens is the macro question AUDD is quietly answering.

cgusd-cygnus-finance.title: Base's Treasury Wrapper
cgusd-cygnus-finance.text: Cygnus Finance's cgUSD is a yield-bearing stablecoin on Base backed by short-term US Treasury Bills, rebasing daily to reflect net asset value. It's the familiar RWA-stablecoin formula -- deposit USDC, get T-bill exposure -- dressed up with Chainlink price feeds and a subsidiary structure under ARKS Labs Foundation. The real test is whether Base users want yet another treasury-yield wrapper when the chain already hosts the issuer of the underlying USDC.

fxusd-f-x-protocol.title: A CDP With Extra Steps
fxusd-f-x-protocol.text: f(x) Protocol's fxUSD is a CDP stablecoin backed by wstETH and WBTC collateral. xPOSITIONs are NFT representations of looped leveraged positions (up to 10x in V2), not a separate volatility-absorbing class. Standard CDP dynamics apply: if leverage demand drops, fxUSD supply contracts naturally without threatening the peg. An f(x) Protocol Stability Pool arbitrages the USDC/fxUSD Curve pool to defend the peg, offering users three sub-strategies: wstETH real yield, fxSAVE autocompound, or FXN gauge rewards.

usdb-blast.title: Blast's Yield Mirage
usdb-blast.text: USDB was Blast L2's headline feature: bridge your stablecoins, get an auto-rebasing dollar token earning yield from MakerDAO's T-bill protocol. In theory, a stablecoin that grows while you hold it. In practice, Blast's TVL collapsed from its peak, and USDB's circulating supply shrank dramatically. The yield mechanics work as advertised; the problem is that the chain built around them failed to retain users after the airdrop farming ended. USDB is now a technically sound product on a chain the market has largely moved on from.

buidl-blackrock.title: When BlackRock Calls It a Token
buidl-blackrock.text: BlackRock's tokenized money market fund is what happens when the world's largest asset manager decides blockchain isn't a meme. BUIDL doesn't try to be a DeFi building block — it's institutional plumbing with an ERC-20 wrapper. When Larry Fink's firm validates tokenization, the rest of TradFi starts returning phone calls.

btcusd-btcfi.title: Bitcoin's CDP Outpost
btcusd-btcfi.text: BtcUSD is a Bitcoin-collateralized stablecoin that leverages cross-chain capabilities to exist across multiple EVM networks. Users deposit WBTC or BTCB into overcollateralized vaults to mint dollars -- a familiar CDP model applied specifically to Bitcoin holders who want liquidity without selling. At its current modest scale, the question is whether BTC holders will trust yet another wrapping layer when established CDPs like MakerDAO already accept wrapped Bitcoin.

gyd-gyroscope.title: The All-Weather Dollar
gyd-gyroscope.text: Gyroscope's GYD is an exercise in paranoid stablecoin design: a diversified reserve of sDAI, USDC, LUSD, and crvUSD, a primary-market AMM that algorithmically adjusts redemption prices during crises, and secondary-market AMMs that concentrate liquidity near the peg. The PAMM's circuit-breaker mechanism -- which reduces redemption rates during bank-run scenarios to preserve solvency -- is elegant game theory. GYD's thesis is that stablecoin design should optimize for surviving tail risks, not maximizing yield.

isc-international-stable-currency.title: The Anti-Dollar Experiment
isc-international-stable-currency.text: ISC deliberately rejects the USD peg in favor of tracking purchasing power through a basket of gold, bonds, T-bills, equities, and cash. The result is a flatcoin that appreciates over time rather than losing value to inflation -- a concept Brian Armstrong has championed but few have actually shipped. At minimal market cap on Solana, ISC is about as niche as stablecoins get. The variable peg and NAV-based pricing make it harder to use as a medium of exchange than a conventional dollar token.

usd0-usual.title: The Usual Suspect
usd0-usual.text: Usual's USD0 burst onto the scene promising a stablecoin where revenue flows back to tokenholders via the USUAL governance token. The RWA-backed reserves provide the peg stability, while the protocol's token economics provide the sizzle. It's an interesting governance experiment, though the December 2024 USD0++ depeg reminded everyone that innovative doesn't mean risk-free.

usr-resolv.title: Resolving the Yield Question
usr-resolv.text: Resolv's USR takes the delta-neutral approach with crypto backing, offering an alternative to Ethena's USDe for users who want basis-trade yields with a different risk profile. Its insurance pool and risk management framework attempt to address the perennial "what happens when funding goes negative" problem. In the basis-trade stablecoin niche, USR competes on risk structure rather than brand recognition.

usdz-anzen.title: Private Credit Meets DeFi
usdz-anzen.text: Anzen's USDz is backed by a private credit portfolio rather than the usual T-bills and cash, tapping into a market that crypto has barely touched. The yield is real, but so is the illiquidity risk inherent in private credit assets. The question every private-credit-backed stablecoin must answer: what happens during a credit crunch when those underlying loans stop performing?

ausd-agora.title: The VanEck-Managed Dollar
ausd-agora.text: Agora's AUSD has the resume that makes compliance departments swoon: VanEck manages the reserves, State Street provides custody, and Chaos Labs delivers real-time proof of reserves with on-chain attestations every 15 minutes. Its revenue-sharing model with distribution partners is the closest thing to a "Stablecoin 3.0" business model anyone has actually shipped. At growing circulation across multiple chains via LayerZero, AUSD is positioning itself as the institutional-grade alternative that doesn't sacrifice DeFi composability.

usds-sky.title: The Artist Formerly Known as DAI
usds-sky.text: Sky Dollar is MakerDAO's rebranded stablecoin, the culmination of Rune Christensen's "Endgame" vision to make the protocol more normie-friendly. Under the hood it's the same overcollateralized vaults and PSM modules — just with a fresh coat of paint and a governance structure that's still figuring itself out. Whether the rebrand was genius marketing or unnecessary complexity remains the market's most polite disagreement.

m-m0.title: The Middleman's Stablecoin
m-m0.text: M0's M token is a middleware play: rather than competing with USDC or USDT directly, it provides infrastructure for other stablecoins and fintechs to build on. Its RWA-backed reserves and centralized-dependent governance aim for a middle ground between Tether's opacity and Circle's centralization. The "protocol for stablecoins" pitch is elegant in theory — the question is whether the market wants a meta-stablecoin layer.

usdm-moneta.title: Cardano's Dollar Anchor
usdm-moneta.text: Moneta's USDM is the premier fiat-backed stablecoin on Cardano, co-issued by Norwegian Block Exchange under an EU e-money license for MiCA compliance. The Charli3 oracle verifying 1:1 reserves before each mint is a thoughtful on-chain guardrail that most stablecoins skip. It's a well-structured product constrained by Cardano's DeFi ecosystem size -- proving once again that the hardest part of launching a stablecoin isn't the backing, it's finding users.

satusd-river.title: The Purist's CDP
satusd-river.text: River's satUSD makes a deliberate choice: no centralized stablecoin collateral accepted, only BTC, ETH, BNB, and LSTs. Its Omni-CDP lets you deposit collateral on one chain and mint on another via LayerZero, eliminating bridge risk. The bull case writes itself -- a pure crypto-collateral CDP with cross-chain reach. The bear case is whether concentrated ecosystem dependencies and the absence of stablecoin collateral create fragility during sharp downturns.

usdf-astherus.title: Binance's Shadow Dollar
usdf-astherus.text: USDF, now under the Aster DEX rebrand, is a yield-bearing stablecoin whose USDT backing is deployed exclusively in delta-neutral strategies on Binance. The yields are attractive, but so is the concentration risk: every dollar of backing runs through Binance infrastructure with Ceffu holding the keys. It's a potent yield machine with a single, very large point of failure.

usda-avalon.title: Bitcoin Banking, On-Chain
usda-avalon.text: Avalon's USDa has quietly become one of the largest CDP projects by TVL, backed by BTC and Bitcoin LSTs with institutional credit lines from Asian conglomerates. The fixed 8% borrowing rate and 1:1 USDT redemption guarantee via institutional liquidity make it structurally distinct from typical CDPs. The CEX-based HFT liquidation engine is clever but means your stablecoin's stability ultimately depends on centralized exchange infrastructure.

usdtb-ethena.title: Ethena's Safe Side
usdtb-ethena.text: If USDe is the exciting sibling, USDtb is the responsible one — backed by BlackRock's BUIDL fund rather than delta-neutral trades. Ethena built it for users who want the ecosystem without the basis-trade risk, creating a safety valve that also serves as USDe's backstop. It's the stablecoin equivalent of keeping a boring index fund alongside your options portfolio.

zeusd-zoth.title: RWA Restaking's First Bet
zeusd-zoth.text: Zoth's ZeUSD bills itself as the first RWA restaking layer -- a CDP stable token minted against tokenized treasuries, ETFs, and money market funds that can then be restaked across DeFi for additional yield. The dual-yield model (off-chain T-bill interest plus on-chain restaking rewards) targets higher returns than vanilla stablecoin staking. Whether "restaking your restaked treasury token" is financial innovation or unnecessary complexity depends on your tolerance for recursive yield engineering.

zchf-frankencoin.title: Swiss Stubbornness, Tokenized
zchf-frankencoin.text: Frankencoin is a genuinely decentralized Swiss franc stablecoin — no foundation, no team tokens, no VC backing. Its auction-based liquidation mechanism and minimalist governance are a throwback to crypto's original ethos. The Swiss franc peg serves a niche audience, but Frankencoin proves that small, well-designed protocols can survive without a marketing budget.

usn-noon.title: The Rotating Yield Engine
usn-noon.text: Noon's USN is a delta-neutral stablecoin that rotates between funding-rate arbitrage and T-bill strategies based on market conditions. The "intelligent allocation" pitch is a more honest framing than most competitors offer -- acknowledging that no single yield source works in all market regimes. Transparent proof of solvency and zero VC pre-allocation is either genuinely aligned or a clever marketing angle; time will tell.

honey-berachain.title: Berachain's Basket Dollar
honey-berachain.text: HONEY is Berachain's native stablecoin, minted by depositing USDC, USDT0, pyUSD, or USDe into per-collateral vaults governed by BGT holders. It's less a novel stablecoin design and more a liquidity unification layer -- aggregating the chain's imported dollars into a single token that serves as Berachain's unit of account. HONEY's fate is entirely coupled to Berachain's success: if the chain's Proof-of-Liquidity model attracts sustained TVL, HONEY thrives as the default dollar; if not, it's just another wrapper nobody asked for.

wusd-worldwide.title: The Payments Play
wusd-worldwide.text: WSPN's Worldwide USD aspires to be the stablecoin for actual commerce, targeting trade finance and cross-border settlements rather than DeFi degens. Its white-label infrastructure lets enterprises issue their own branded stablecoins, which is either a clever platform play or an admission that WUSD itself lacks distribution. The market cap remains modest despite partnerships spanning Philippines exchanges to Australian commodity exporters, suggesting the "stablecoin payment network" thesis is still more pitch deck than protocol.

frxusd-frax.title: Frax Grows Up
frxusd-frax.text: After years of algorithmic experimentation that made regulators nervous and degens rich, Frax Finance went full TradFi with frxUSD -- a fully-backed stablecoin whose reserves sit in BlackRock's BUIDL fund, tokenized by Securitize. The DAO voted unanimously for the pivot, which tells you everything about where crypto's risk appetite has shifted. Sam Kazemian's stated ambition of applying for a Federal Reserve Master Account is either visionary or delusional, but the BlackRock backing lends it more credibility than most stablecoin founders' dreams.

usyc-hashnote.title: Treasury Yields On-Chain
usyc-hashnote.text: Hashnote's USYC is a tokenized money market fund that passes T-bill yields directly to holders. It's RWA-backed, yield-bearing, and about as exciting as its underlying asset — which is precisely the point. In a world of exotic DeFi yields, sometimes the most radical product is just a savings account with an ERC-20 wrapper.

eurr-stablr.title: Malta's Euro Bet
eurr-stablr.text: StablR's EURR is one of the early MiCA-compliant euro stablecoins, licensed through Malta's MFSA and backed by Tether's strategic investment -- a move that lets Tether maintain European presence without doing the compliance work itself. Grant Thornton audits and The Network Firm proof-of-reserves add credibility layers, though the real question is whether a Tether-backed entity can win institutional trust in a market built on regulatory purity.

usdr-stablr.title: The Dollar Sibling
usdr-stablr.text: StablR's USDR rides the same Malta EMI license and MiCA compliance infrastructure as its euro sibling EURR, offering a dollar-denominated option for European users who want regulatory certainty. Reserves sit with European financial institutions in cash and short-term government bonds, audited by Grant Thornton. It is a competent, regulation-first product in a market that increasingly rewards exactly that -- though differentiating a compliant USD stablecoin in a field of dozens remains the core challenge.

usdo-openeden.title: Treasury Yield, Repackaged
usdo-openeden.text: OpenEden's USDO is a regulated yield-bearing stablecoin with a Bermuda BMA license and TBILL-token backing that gives it genuine substance. The rebasing mechanism distributes T-bill yield daily by increasing holder balances -- elegant for retail, awkward for DeFi protocols that don't handle rebasing tokens, hence the cUSDO wrapper. Crossing $100M TVL within months of launch suggests the market has an appetite for transparent, tokenized-treasury stablecoins that aren't just institutional playthings.

usda-anzens.title: Cardano's Dollar, Finally
usda-anzens.text: USDA has been the stablecoin Cardano needed but couldn't quite ship, delayed by regulatory headwinds and operational handoffs. It finally went live with BitGo custody and no mint/burn fees. For a blockchain ecosystem that has long been criticized for lacking stablecoin infrastructure, USDA is a necessary step -- though limited U.S. state availability at launch suggests the regulatory path is far from complete.

usdf-falcon.title: The Falcon Play
usdf-falcon.text: Falcon Finance's USDf enters the delta-neutral arena alongside Ethena, offering yield through basis-trade strategies with a centralized-dependent governance model. Its crypto-backed structure means the peg relies on market dynamics rather than reserve transparency. In the crowded yield-bearing stablecoin space, differentiation is a question of execution speed and risk management.

europ-schuman.title: France's MiCA Pioneer
europ-schuman.text: Schuman Financial's EUROP is what happens when you build a euro stablecoin with the Banque de France looking over your shoulder. ACPR-licensed, KPMG-audited, and reserves held at Societe Generale, it checks every institutional box that MiCA demands -- plus an extra 2% reserve buffer beyond the 1:1 requirement. With euro stablecoins representing barely a fraction of the global stablecoin float, even the best-credentialed entrant faces a market that simply hasn't arrived yet.

brz-transfero.title: Latin America's Bridge
brz-transfero.text: Brazilian Digital's BRZ gives Brazil's crypto traders a real-denominated on-ramp without the volatility of converting through USD pairs. RWA-backed and centrally managed, it serves a practical need in one of crypto's most active retail markets. Its success is less about innovation and more about understanding that sometimes the simplest product wins.

rlusd-ripple.title: Ripple's Dollar Bet
rlusd-ripple.text: After years of fighting the SEC over XRP, Ripple launched its own stablecoin with NYDFS approval — a plot twist even Ripple skeptics didn't see coming. RLUSD is built for Ripple's payments network, aiming to be the bridge asset that XRP never became for institutional transfers. Fully reserved and centrally managed, it's less a DeFi primitive and more a cross-border payments tool.

feusd-felix.title: Hyperliquid's Lending Layer
feusd-felix.text: Felix Protocol forked Liquity V2 and deployed it on Hyperliquid L1, creating a CDP-based stablecoin that lets traders mint feUSD against HYPE, WBTC, ETH, and LSTs to use as margin. Growth from zero to substantial deposits within months is impressive, though much of it is inseparable from Hyperliquid's own ecosystem momentum. The Liquity-derived architecture adds proven liquidation mechanics, but the addition of centralized admin controls -- mint caps, emergency pausing -- means this is very much a modified fork, not a philosophical successor.

dusd-standx.title: Delta-Neutral via CeFi
dusd-standx.text: StandX's DUSD takes the Ethena playbook -- spot long, perps short, pocket the spread -- and runs it through centralized custodians and its own perpetual futures DEX. The team's Binance Futures and Goldman Sachs pedigree explains the institutional architecture: off-chain collateral management with exchange-provided leverage and strict margin controls. Any delta-neutral stablecoin is ultimately a bet that funding rates remain favorable more often than not.

eurcv-societe-generale-forge.title: SocGen's Blockchain Experiment
eurcv-societe-generale-forge.text: EUR CoinVertible is issued by SG-FORGE, the digital asset arm of French banking giant Société Générale. It's a fully regulated, MiCA-compliant euro stablecoin from a systemically important bank — which is either the future of tokenized money or a corporate innovation lab's pet project. Either way, when a bank with over a trillion euros in assets issues a stablecoin, the industry takes notes.

yusd-aegis.title: Bitcoin-Margined Stability
yusd-aegis.text: Aegis's YUSD markets itself as a bitcoin-backed stablecoin independent from fiat banking, which is a bold framing for what is essentially a delta-neutral strategy using BTC-margined perpetual contracts. The real-time proof-of-reserves through Accountable's verification network is genuinely differentiated -- you can watch the custodial vaults and open positions in real time, which is more than most competitors offer. Its survival depends on the same funding-rate dynamics that govern every delta-neutral stablecoin.

reusd-resupply.title: Curve's Recursive Dollar
reusd-resupply.text: Resupply's reUSD, built by the Convex and Yearn teams, is a stablecoin for crvUSD power users who want to leverage their lending positions further. Deposit crvUSD into Curve Lend, use the position as collateral, mint reUSD, sell it for more crvUSD, repeat. It pushed crvUSD to all-time-high supply -- a testament to recursive DeFi appetite. The composability that makes reUSD powerful is the same composability that makes it fragile.

tbill-openeden.title: The Original T-Bill Token
tbill-openeden.text: OpenEden's TBILL is a tokenized money market fund with institutional-grade ratings, managed by BNY Investments. Access is restricted to KYC'd professional investors, which limits retail appeal but is precisely the point. At competitive APY on short-dated treasuries, TBILL is less a stablecoin and more a regulated fund that happens to be an ERC-20 -- and for its target audience, that distinction matters.

a7a5-old-vector.title: The Ruble's Digital Shadow
a7a5-old-vector.text: A7A5 is a ruble-pegged stablecoin that appeared seemingly from nowhere to claim a massive market cap. Its centralized governance and RWA backing make it structurally conventional, but the geopolitical context makes it anything but. In a sanctions-heavy environment, a large ruble stablecoin raises more questions than its sparse documentation answers.

usd1-world-liberty-financial.title: The Presidential Stablecoin
usd1-world-liberty-financial.text: World Liberty Financial's USD1 is backed by the Trump family brand and entered the market with all the subtlety you'd expect. It launched with RWA backing and centralized governance, positioning itself somewhere between a political statement and a financial product. The reserves are real, but the regulatory questions write themselves.

usdx-hex-trust.title: Hong Kong's Quiet Dollar
usdx-hex-trust.text: Hex Trust's USDX is built by one of Asia's most established digital asset custodians, licensed under Hong Kong's TCSP regime with reserves in short-term Treasury Bills. Its primary home is the Flare blockchain and the newer Ozean chain, where it doubles as the native gas token -- an unusual dual role for a stablecoin. With 270+ institutional clients and offices across five countries, Hex Trust has the distribution network; whether USDX can translate custodial relationships into stablecoin adoption is the open question.

pusd-plume.title: Plume's Wrapped Dollar
pusd-plume.text: pUSD is a straightforward USDC wrapper on Plume Chain, held 1:1 in a BoringVault with zero minting or redemption fees. It exists to give Plume's RWAfi ecosystem a canonical stablecoin without building reserve infrastructure from scratch -- pragmatic if unambitious. The integration of World Liberty Financial's USD1 as an additional reserve asset adds political flavor to what is otherwise a utilitarian design.

bold-liquity.title: Decentralization, Immutable
bold-liquity.text: Liquity V2's BOLD is the stablecoin for people who mean it when they say decentralized. No governance, no upgrades, no RWA exposure -- just ETH and liquid staking tokens in overcollateralized vaults with user-set interest rates. The immutability is a feature and a constraint: any bug discovered post-deployment requires a full redeployment. The yield amplification mechanic, where stability pool depositors can earn more than borrowers pay, is clever game theory that sets BOLD apart from the lending-market stablecoin crowd.

avusd-avant.title: Avalanche's Quiet Contender
avusd-avant.text: Avant's avUSD is a USDC-backed stable-value token on Avalanche that pairs with savUSD, its yield-bearing counterpart running DeFi-native strategies including cash-and-carry trades. Growing to significant value within its first year with zero management fees suggests competent execution, even if the value proposition -- deposit USDC, get a wrapped version, optionally earn yield -- isn't going to set anyone's imagination on fire. In the Avalanche ecosystem, being the default stable-value token is a defensible position, if a modest one.

ylds-figure.title: The SEC-Registered Yield Coin
ylds-figure.text: YLDS stands alone as one of the few yield-bearing stablecoins registered with the SEC as a security. This means actual regulatory clarity rather than the "move fast and hope for the best" approach most competitors take. The trade-off is operational constraints and restricted availability, but for institutions requiring regulatory certainty, YLDS is the rare stablecoin that comes with a blessing from Washington.

usdq-quantoz.title: The Dutch Compliance Standard
usdq-quantoz.text: Quantoz's USDQ holds the distinction of being issued from the only MiCA-licensed stablecoin jurisdiction with a AAA credit rating, supervised by De Nederlandsche Bank itself. Backed by Tether, Kraken, and Fabric Ventures, it combines institutional credibility with the pragmatic observation that European crypto users need dollar-denominated stablecoins too. The Visa principal membership for stablecoin-linked debit cards is the kind of distribution play that turns compliance into competitive advantage.

usdn-noble.title: The Interchain Dollar
usdn-noble.text: Noble's USDN is built on M0's stablecoin extension engine, making it a white-labeled version of M0's treasury-backed M token designed specifically for the Cosmos ecosystem. The yield-distribution model passes T-bill returns to holders, validators, and supporting platforms, creating incentive alignment that most stablecoins ignore entirely. Noble has already facilitated billions in stablecoin transfers across Cosmos, so the distribution infrastructure is proven. Whether the IBC-native approach can compete beyond Cosmos is the strategic gamble.

usdu-unitas.title: The JLP Hedge Fund
usdu-unitas.text: Unitas routes your USDC deposits into Jupiter LP tokens and hedges the spot exposure with CEX perpetual shorts -- a delta-neutral strategy that sounds like a hedge fund pitch deck because it basically is one. Custody sits with Ceffu and Copper via off-exchange settlement, which limits exchange counterparty risk but doesn't eliminate it. When funding rates flip negative for an extended period, the entire yield thesis inverts. Still, the zero-knowledge solvency proofs are a genuine transparency upgrade over the "trust us" school of crypto yield products.

mnee-mnee.title: BSV's Dollar Envoy
mnee-mnee.text: MNEE is a fiat-backed stablecoin issued under an Antigua and Barbuda FSRC digital asset license -- a jurisdiction that doesn't exactly scream regulatory gravitas. Originally launched on BSV (yes, that BSV), it has since expanded to ERC-20, suggesting the team recognized that ecosystem size matters more than block size ideology. Backed by US Treasury bills, cash, and stablecoin equivalents with regular attestations. The regulatory framework is real, even if Antigua's FSRC ranks somewhere below the SEC and MAS in the global credibility hierarchy.

usdg-paxos.title: The Paxos Sequel
usdg-paxos.text: Global Dollar is Paxos's second act after BUSD, built to avoid the regulatory friction that killed its Binance partnership. Singapore-regulated and reserve-backed, USDG targets the institutional corridor that doesn't want Tether's opacity or Circle's SVB memories. Whether the market needs another compliant stablecoin is a question USDG is determined to answer anyway.

xsgd-straitsx.title: Singapore's DeFi On-Ramp
xsgd-straitsx.text: XSGD is one of the few non-USD stablecoins with genuine regulatory credentials, operating under Singapore's MAS Major Payment Institution framework with reserves at DBS and Standard Chartered. Five years in, it has processed billions in combined on-chain volume with XUSD and expanded to seven-plus chains. The Grab partnership and OKX Pay integration signal that StraitsX is building for real-world payments, not just DeFi yield farming. A rare case of a non-dollar stablecoin that might actually matter.

xusd-straitsx.title: Singapore's Dollar Export
xusd-straitsx.text: XUSD is StraitsX's USD-pegged sibling to XSGD, sharing the same MAS regulatory framework and Tier-1 banking reserves. The infrastructure story is compelling: bimonthly independent attestations, multi-chain deployment, and planned cross-currency pairing with XSGD for Southeast Asian payment corridors. The real differentiator isn't the backing -- it's the same as every other compliant USD stablecoin -- but the regional focus on SGD-USD forex flows.

vgbp-vnx.title: Sterling on the Blockchain
vgbp-vnx.text: VNX's VGBP is one of vanishingly few GBP-pegged stablecoins on the market, issued under Liechtenstein's Blockchain Act with reserves in Swiss and Liechtenstein banks. The fourth most-traded fiat currency in the world has surprisingly little on-chain representation, giving VGBP an open field with almost no competition. Available on Solana, Base, and Celo, though liquidity remains thin.

cusd-cap.title: Cap's Yield Play
cusd-cap.text: Cap Protocol's cUSD offers an RWA-backed stablecoin with a centralized-dependent governance model that routes yield back to holders. It operates in the increasingly crowded space of yield-bearing stablecoins, competing on distribution and integration rather than novelty. The protocol's bet is that a well-executed yield product can carve out space between the giants.

msusd-main-street.title: Volatility Arbitrage in a Wrapper
msusd-main-street.text: Main Street USD takes the Ethena playbook and swaps basis trades for options volatility arbitrage -- betting that machine learning models can consistently identify mispriced implied volatility. The claimed high APY would be extraordinary in tradfi, which should calibrate your skepticism accordingly. For a product marketing institutional-grade strategies, the broad owner upgrade authority on the proxy contract means the trust assumptions are decidedly retail-grade.

iusd-infinifi.title: Private Credit, Public Interface
iusd-infinifi.text: InfiniFi's pitch hasn't changed — fractional reserve USDC vault, tiered lock-ups for tiered yield — but what's in the vault has. The portfolio that once ran on Ethena sUSDe and Pendle PTs now deploys 80% of its $171M into institutional private credit: Fasanara Capital at 9% APY, FalconX prime brokerage at 6.25%, Sentora's PYUSD strategy at 6%. The liquid 20% exists to service redemptions, not generate returns. This is less DeFi yield aggregator and more on-chain credit fund with a tiered savings product on top. The 5.4% siUSD APY is real because the underlying credit risk is real, and the adequacy of a $33M liquid buffer against a $171M book is ultimately a function of how many users check their lock-up terms before they need cash.

pht-pht.title: Peso Stablecoin Pioneer
pht-pht.text: PHT is a Philippine peso-pegged stablecoin built on a MakerDAO MCD fork, overcollateralized by USDC and USDT vaults. It's targeting the $38 billion Filipino remittance corridor where traditional fees eat 6%+ of every transfer. The technical architecture is sound -- MCD is battle-tested -- but adoption for local-currency stablecoins requires merchant integration and fiat off-ramps that raw DeFi infrastructure doesn't provide. A worthy experiment in local-currency stablecoins for a market that desperately needs cheaper money movement.

hyusd-hylo.title: Solana's Native Stable
hyusd-hylo.text: Hylo's hyUSD is backed entirely by yield-bearing Solana liquid staking tokens -- mSOL, jitoSOL, and bSOL -- with no fiat reserves, no RWAs, and no centralized dependencies. The dual-token design uses xSOL to absorb volatility, maintaining 160%+ overcollateralization while offering leveraged SOL exposure without liquidation risk. The oracle-free design is elegant in theory, but the entire system inherits validator slashing risk and LST depeg risk from its collateral basket.

meusd-mezo.title: Bitcoin's Debt Position
meusd-mezo.text: Mezo's meUSD is what happens when Bitcoin maximalists discover CDPs. Backed exclusively by BTC with a minimum 110% collateral ratio, it's the purest expression of Bitcoin-native DeFi -- no ETH, no stablecoins, just sats in a vault. Built on Mezo's Bitcoin L2 with EVM compatibility and tBTC bridging, the protocol leverages Liquity-style redemption mechanics to maintain peg stability. The 110% minimum collateral ratio is aggressive for an asset as volatile as Bitcoin, though typical user ratios hover higher.

usdu-usdu-finance.title: The Adapter Stablecoin
usdu-usdu-finance.text: USDU Finance takes a modular approach to stablecoin design, where protocol-minted tokens can only be created through DAO-approved adapters connected to Curve, Morpho, and TermMax vaults. All backing is held as adapter-owned LP tokens and vault shares, not user balances -- a meaningful structural distinction from most stablecoins. The Curve adapter dynamically adds or removes liquidity based on pool imbalance, while TermMax enables fixed-rate lending for RWA collateral.

uty-xsy.title: Avalanche's Ethena
uty-xsy.text: XSY's Unity (UTY) applies the delta-neutral playbook to AVAX: long spot, short perps, collect the spread. Founded by veterans from Algorand, Paxos, and Floating Point Group, it's the highest-pedigree attempt to build a synthetic dollar native to Avalanche. Whether the AVAX perpetual futures market has sufficient depth and consistent positive funding to sustain this model long-term remains the central question.

gusd-gate.title: Exchange Scrip, RWA Edition
gusd-gate.text: Gate's GUSD is a yield-bearing stablecoin that functions more like an investment certificate than a medium of exchange. Backed by US Treasuries, exchange revenue, and stablecoin yield strategies, it offers annualized returns that accrue silently until redemption. The platform promises to "gradually disclose reserve proofs" -- a phrase that inspires exactly as much confidence as it should. Useful within Gate's walled garden, less so as a general-purpose stablecoin.

usdcv-societe-generale-forge.title: A Bank's Stablecoin
usdcv-societe-generale-forge.text: SG-FORGE's USDCV is the first USD stablecoin issued by a major European bank, with BNY as reserve custodian and full MiCA compliance from day one. Licensed as an EMI by France's ACPR, it represents what happens when a 160-year-old bank decides to issue tokens on Ethereum. Daily reserve disclosure and institutional-grade custody make it arguably the most regulated stablecoin in existence. The catch: US persons are explicitly excluded, making it a European product that denominates in dollars it can't sell to Americans.

usdai-usd-ai.title: AI Meets RWA
usdai-usd-ai.text: USD.AI blends the two hottest crypto narratives — artificial intelligence and real-world assets — into a single stablecoin product. Its centralized-dependent governance suggests human oversight where it counts, while the AI branding does the marketing work. Whether the "AI" label reflects genuine innovation or narrative arbitrage is left as an exercise for the reader.

usx-solstice.title: The Swiss Yield Vault
usx-solstice.text: Solstice's USX combines delta-neutral strategies across BTC, ETH, and SOL with tokenized treasuries and fiat stablecoin reserves, all verified by Chainlink Proof of Reserve. Run by Solstice Labs AG out of Zug, Switzerland, with custody via Ceffu and Copper, it launched with significant TVL and backing from Galaxy Digital and Susquehanna. The strong track record with zero negative months is the kind of performance that makes allocators salivate and risk managers nervous.

hollar-hydrated.title: Polkadot's Home Dollar
hollar-hydrated.text: HOLLAR is Hydration's overcollateralized stablecoin, backed by DOT, ETH, WBTC, USDT, USDC, and LSTs on Polkadot's largest DeFi protocol. The Stability Module draws inspiration from Aave's GHO, and partial liquidations at the protocol level are a thoughtful design choice. With a conservative initial supply cap and controlled borrow rate, Hydration is clearly prioritizing controlled growth over aggressive expansion -- a rare display of restraint in DeFi.

musd-metamask.title: The Wallet Becomes the Bank
musd-metamask.text: MetaMask's mUSD is what happens when the world's most popular self-custodial wallet decides 30 million monthly users should have their own stablecoin. Issued by Stripe's Bridge using M0 protocol, with Blackstone managing treasury reserves in bankruptcy-remote accounts holding T-bills. The distribution advantage is enormous -- mUSD is native to the wallet where most DeFi users already live. Plans for yield sharing and MetaMask Card spending at Mastercard merchants signal ambitions well beyond DeFi.

cash-phantom.title: Yield Rebase on Polygon
cash-phantom.text: Stabl.fi's CASH is a yield-generating stable indexcoin on Polygon that mints against USDC, USDT, and DAI deposits, then deploys those assets across chains and protocols to generate organic yield distributed via rebases. The concept is sound -- automated yield aggregation with a stable denomination. The execution has been less encouraging: thin trading volume and persistent below-peg pricing suggest the peg mechanism isn't exactly thriving. CASH reads like a DeFi experiment that never quite found its audience.

tgbp-tokenised.title: Sterling's Lone Ranger
tgbp-tokenised.text: BCP Technologies' tGBP holds the distinction of being the UK's first FCA-registered GBP stablecoin, having graduated from the regulatory sandbox. With a small market cap, it's less a dominant force and more a proof of concept for sterling on-chain. The Wirex integration brought it to millions of potential users, but GBP stablecoins collectively remain a rounding error in a dollar-dominated market. Its real significance lies in being the regulatory template that every subsequent UK stablecoin issuer will be measured against.

eurau-allunity.title: Deutsche Boerse's Euro Bet
eurau-allunity.text: AllUnity's EURAU is what happens when DWS, Galaxy, and Flow Traders decide Europe needs a proper MiCA-compliant euro stablecoin. Licensed by BaFin as an electronic money institution and already integrated into Deutsche Boerse's Clearstream infrastructure, it carries more institutional credibility than most euro stablecoins combined. The problem is the denominator: euro stablecoins represent roughly 0.2% of the global stablecoin market, making EURAU both a success story and a reminder of how thoroughly the dollar dominates this space.

usdh-native-markets.title: Hyperliquid's Chosen One
usdh-native-markets.text: Native Markets beat Paxos, Ethena, and Frax in a validator vote to become Hyperliquid's native stablecoin issuer, despite offering a less generous revenue split. The win was about ecosystem alignment over financial incentives -- validators preferred a builder who understood the platform over incumbents waving larger checks. With reserves managed by BlackRock and custody via Anchorage, the backing is institutional-grade, but the real play is capturing the yield from Hyperliquid's USDC deposits that currently flows to Circle.

sbc-brale.title: The Plumber's Stablecoin
sbc-brale.text: Brale's SBC is less a consumer-facing stablecoin and more a demonstration of what Brale's stablecoin-as-a-service platform can do. Built by Dwolla's founder and backed by straightforward cash and treasuries under US money transmitter licenses, it optimizes for boring reliability over yield. The real product is Brale itself -- the infrastructure layer that lets other companies issue their own compliant stablecoins across 20-plus chains. SBC is the reference implementation; the clients are the business.

euri-banking-circle.title: Binance's Euro
euri-banking-circle.text: Eurite is the euro stablecoin endorsed by Binance, giving it instant distribution to the world's largest exchange. Issued by Banking Circle and regulated in the EU, it's MiCA-ready from day one. Whether Binance's distribution muscle can make a euro stablecoin stick where others have struggled remains the open question.

msusd-metronome.title: Synths Still Standing
msusd-metronome.text: Metronome's msUSD is a synthetic dollar from the pre-yield-farming era that somehow kept its peg and its users. Minted against productive collateral like Vesper pool tokens, it offers zero-slippage swaps against other Metronome synths -- a neat trick in a market where synthetic assets have largely fallen out of fashion. The 18% liquidation penalty ensures borrowers stay overcollateralized, which is another way of saying the protocol learned from 2022.

aznd-mu-digital.title: Asia Credit Goes On-Chain
aznd-mu-digital.text: Mu Digital's AZND tokenizes senior-tranche Asian credit instruments to offer 6-7% native yield, targeting a market that has historically been reserved for institutional desks and private banks. The dual-tranche structure with muBOND absorbing first losses to protect AZND holders is sound credit engineering. The question is whether DeFi users accustomed to double-digit yields will find single-digit returns from Asian corporates compelling enough to bridge the trust gap.

nect-beraborrow.title: Berachain's Liquity Fork
nect-beraborrow.text: BeraBorrow's NECT is a Liquity-style CDP stablecoin purpose-built for Berachain, accepting the chain's native menagerie of liquid staking derivatives as collateral. With an exclusive license to deploy Liquity V2 on Berachain, it has positioned itself as the chain's foundational lending primitive. The auto-compounding dens that reinvest rewards into collateral are a clever twist on the CDP model, reducing liquidation risk while keeping users engaged. Whether NECT becomes Berachain's canonical dollar depends entirely on whether Berachain itself achieves escape velocity.

usp-pikudao.title: Turkish Carry Trade, Tokenized
usp-pikudao.text: PikuDAO's USP is a yield-bearing stablecoin that appreciates over time rather than maintaining a fixed peg, with half its backing deployed into a Turkish lira FX arbitrage strategy. The logic is simple: Turkey's high inflation creates persistent demand for dollar-denominated assets, and Balsa Technologies captures the spread through delta-neutral TRY-USD trades. It's a genuinely novel yield source for DeFi -- uncorrelated with crypto markets -- but also one that concentrates geopolitical and counterparty risk in a single emerging market.

pmusd-precious-metals.title: Gold-Backed With Extra Steps
pmusd-precious-metals.text: RAAC's pmUSD routes tokenized gold from I-ON Digital through overcollateralized CDPs to produce a dollar-pegged stablecoin with precious metal backing. Chainlink Proof of Reserves and Instruxi attestations add transparency layers. The gap between announced gold tokenization capacity and actual circulating supply is the kind of detail that separates press releases from products.

jupusd-jupiter.title: Jupiter's BlackRock Dollar
jupusd-jupiter.text: JupUSD is Jupiter's bid to own the dollar layer on Solana, backed 90% by Ethena's USDtb -- which itself holds BlackRock's BUIDL fund shares. The plan to convert hundreds of millions of JLP's USDC holdings into JupUSD is as much a revenue play as a product launch: every dollar moved from USDC to JupUSD is yield redirected from Circle to Jupiter's ecosystem. Anchorage Digital handles custody, Ethena manages reserves, and Jupiter gets to call it native. It's a well-executed supply-chain integration disguised as a stablecoin.

u-united-stables.title: The Aggregator Dollar
u-united-stables.text: United Stables takes the yield-aggregation approach, pooling reserves across multiple strategies and passing the returns to holders. It's a bet that diversification of stablecoin backing is itself a feature worth tokenizing. Simple concept, hard execution.

reusd-re-protocol.title: Reinsurance Meets DeFi
reusd-re-protocol.text: Re Protocol's reUSD channels stablecoin deposits into actual quota-share reinsurance contracts, generating yield from insurance premiums rather than trading or lending. The principal-protected structure targets risk-free-rate-plus-250-basis-points, which sounds pedestrian until you consider the yield is uncorrelated with crypto markets. It's the rare DeFi product where "real yield" actually means real yield.

rwausdi-multipli.title: The RWA Middleware Layer
rwausdi-multipli.text: Multipli.fi's rwaUSDi attempts to solve DeFi's fragmentation problem for tokenized real-world assets by creating a unified collateral token that wraps treasuries, gold, and other RWAs into a single mintable unit. The pitch is that lending protocols like Aave and Morpho can't individually underwrite thousands of tokenized assets, so rwaUSDi does the due diligence for them. It's an elegant abstraction layer, though one that adds another trust assumption between the user and the underlying assets.

pusd-pleasing.title: Hong Kong Gold, Arbitrum Rails
pusd-pleasing.text: Pleasing International's PUSD is a synthetic dollar backed by USDT reserves with tokenized gold exposure through PGOLD, deployed on Arbitrum. The Hong Kong-based precious metals firm is targeting the Asia-Middle East gold corridor. But PUSD's hybrid reserve structure -- part stablecoin collateral, part commodity exposure -- means it's neither a pure dollar peg nor a gold-backed token, occupying an awkward middle ground that may confuse more than it attracts.

usdm-mega.title: Funding the Sequencer
usdm-mega.text: MegaETH's USDm flips the L2 business model: instead of extracting sequencer fees from users, it uses reserve yield from Ethena's USDtb to subsidize network operations. It's a clever alignment trick -- the chain literally gets cheaper as more people hold its native stablecoin. Backed by BlackRock's BUIDL via the USDtb stack, the reserves are institutional-grade, though the dependency on Ethena's infrastructure adds a layer of counterparty risk. The economics reveal a flywheel where stablecoin adoption drives token value drives adoption.

usat-tether.title: Tether Comes Home
usat-tether.text: After years of operating from the British Virgin Islands, Tether launched a US-regulated stablecoin through Anchorage Digital Bank under the GENIUS Act. USA-T is the clearest signal yet that Tether views domestic regulation as a market to capture rather than a threat to avoid. The dual-product strategy -- USAT for US compliance, USDT for global liquidity -- is Tether's answer to Circle's home-turf advantage, backed by billions in annual revenue and an explicit goal of massive scale.

yzusd-yuzu.title: Yield Vault in Stable Clothing
yzusd-yuzu.text: Yuzu Money's yzUSD packages curated DeFi yield strategies into an overcollateralized stablecoin, with Accountable providing real-time proof of solvency and Hypernative handling threat detection. The strict KYC gating -- only accredited, qualified, or institutional investors can mint and redeem -- makes it one of the most access-restricted stablecoins in DeFi. It's a yield aggregator that happens to maintain a dollar peg rather than a stablecoin that happens to generate yield. The distinction matters when things go wrong.

nusd-neutrl.title: OTC Discounts, Tokenized
nusd-neutrl.text: Neutrl's NUSD monetizes the gap between OTC-discounted locked tokens and their spot market value, hedging directional exposure with perpetual futures shorts. Through its relationship with STIX, it accesses venture token allocations at 30-70% discounts -- a trade that hedge funds have run for years but DeFi users couldn't access. The strategy's capacity is inherently limited by OTC deal flow, but Neutrl is betting that the massive token unlock overhang provides years of raw material.

usdgo-osl.title: Asia's On-Ramp Dollar
usdgo-osl.text: OSL Group's USDGO pairs a Hong Kong-listed company's distribution network with Anchorage Digital's US federal bank charter, creating a stablecoin built for the Asia-to-US institutional corridor. GENIUS Act compliance and the Anchorage relationship give it solid regulatory credentials, though OSL's focus on e-commerce, gaming, and trade settlement targets a narrower but potentially more defensible niche than general-purpose competitors.

fidd-fidelity.title: Fidelity's Trillion-Dollar Entrance
fidd-fidelity.text: When the third-largest asset manager on earth launches a stablecoin, the signal matters more than the product. FIDD is textbook institutional: reserves at BNY Mellon, PwC attestations, OCC national trust charter, daily NAV disclosure that exceeds Circle's monthly cadence. Fidelity's distribution moat -- retail through Fidelity Crypto, institutional through Fidelity Digital Assets, and advisors through its wealth platform -- gives FIDD access to channels that crypto-native issuers can only dream about. Underestimating Fidelity's distribution muscle would be unwise.

aid-gaib.title: GPU Yield, Dollarized
aid-gaib.text: GAIB's AID is a conventional dollar stablecoin — T-bills and stablecoin reserves, 1:1 mint and burn — whose entire reason for existing is its companion token sAID, which accrues yield from GPU and AI infrastructure financing deals. The structure neatly separates stable value (AID) from exotic yield (sAID), letting users choose their risk exposure. At $21 million market cap it's early-stage even by RWA standards, betting that AI compute demand will create a durable yield substrate. Whether GPU financing agreements produce reliable enough cash flows to back a yield product is genuinely untested — but in a market where every new stablecoin needs a narrative, "AI infrastructure yield" is at least more substantive than most.

apxusd-apyx.title: Dividends as Collateral
apxusd-apyx.text: Apyx introduced what might be the most creative collateral backing in stablecoins: preferred shares from Digital Asset Treasury companies — publicly traded equity from firms like Strategy that hold large crypto positions. The theory is that variable-rate preferred shares trade near par regardless of crypto price volatility, providing stable collateral for a dollar token. Launched on Ethereum in February 2026 with DeFi Development Corp as an early investor, apxUSD is so new that market cap data barely exists. The Protocol-Owned Liquidity buffer is meant to absorb stress, but the underlying question is whether equity dividends from crypto-holding companies are truly uncorrelated with the crypto market they depend on.

jpyc-jpyc.title: The Yen's Licensed Pioneer
jpyc-jpyc.text: Japan's first FSA-approved yen stablecoin occupies an enviable regulatory position — Type II Funds Transfer license, 100% JGB-backed reserves, zero transaction fees — and a laughable market cap of $17 million. JPYC Inc. has set a 10-trillion-yen target that would require 3,400x growth, which is either visionary ambition or Japanese corporate optimism at its finest. The real threat isn't GYEN (regulated in New York but locked out of Japan's domestic market) but Progmat Coin, a joint venture from Mitsubishi UFJ, Sumitomo Mitsui, and Mizuho — three megabanks whose combined balance sheet makes JPYC look like a rounding error. Being first to market matters less when the second movers have trillion-dollar balance sheets.

xaut-tether.title: Tether Mints Bullion
xaut-tether.text: Tether's gold token commands half the $6 billion tokenized gold market, which sounds impressive until you notice that share was 60% six months ago. XAUT works exactly like you'd expect from Tether: BDO Italia attestations, undisclosed Swiss custodian, El Salvador jurisdiction, and a market that trades on brand recognition over transparency. The real story is that Tether bought 27 tons of physical gold in 2025, making it one of the larger non-sovereign gold accumulators — the tokenized wrapper is almost an afterthought. With gold's 65% rally inflating all boats, the question is whether XAUT's eroding market share matters when the pie keeps growing.

paxg-paxos.title: Fort Knox With a Charter
paxg-paxos.text: The only federally regulated gold token in existence, PAXG operates under Paxos's OCC national trust charter with KPMG monthly attestations and allocated bars at Brink's London. At $2.5 billion it holds roughly 40% of the tokenized gold market — the permanent second to Tether Gold, but the first choice for anyone whose compliance department has veto power. While XAUT trades on Tether's distribution, PAXG trades on verifiable custody: allocated bars with serial numbers, bankruptcy-remote trust structure, and the kind of regulatory paper trail that makes institutional allocators comfortable. In a market where gold itself is the product, trust infrastructure is the only real differentiator.

kau-kinesis.title: Gold That Pays Rent
kau-kinesis.text: Kinesis cracked the code that other gold tokens missed: people want yield. KAU holders earn a share of 15% of all platform transaction fees, paid monthly in additional gold — a model that propelled it from negligible to 8% market share in just twelve weeks. At $388 million it's still dwarfed by the XAUT-PAXG duopoly, but the trajectory is the story. Add a virtual Mastercard for point-of-sale gold spending and you get something genuinely different: gold that functions as money, not just an asset. The catch is that yield depends entirely on Kinesis's transaction volume — if trading dries up, so does the rent check.

xaum-matrixdock.title: Asia's Institutional Bullion
xaum-matrixdock.text: Matrixdock's gold token sits at $70 million — a rounding error next to XAUT and PAXG — but its strategy is infrastructure, not retail. Bureau Veritas-audited bars in Singapore and Hong Kong vaults, a February 2026 expansion to Solana, and a partnership with Bhutan's Gelephu Mindfulness City for sovereign gold tokenization all point to the same thesis: institutional RWA rails for Asia-Pacific. Whether XAUm becomes the region's gold standard or remains a well-audited footnote depends on whether institutions actually prefer Asia-domiciled custody over London and Swiss vaults.

gold-vro.title: Gold in the Free Ports
gold-vro.text: VeraOne stores its gold in the Geneva Free Ports — the same duty-free Swiss storage complex favored by art collectors and sovereign wealth funds — which gives VRO perhaps the most interesting custody story in tokenized gold and absolutely none of the liquidity to match. At $48 million market cap with minimal trading volume, it's a micro-cap gold gram token that proves having premium vault infrastructure doesn't automatically attract premium capital. The 1 VRO = 1 gram denomination makes it accessible on paper, but without meaningful exchange listings or DeFi integrations, accessibility remains theoretical.

cgo-comtech.title: DMCC-Stamped Bullion
cgo-comtech.text: Dubai's contribution to tokenized gold arrives with serious pedigree: DMCC endorsement, Transguard vault custody under the Emirates Group umbrella, individually serialized 24-karat bars registered on DMCC Tradeflow, and a sleek redemption-via-app workflow. At $18 million market cap, none of that pedigree has translated into meaningful adoption. CGO occupies the same awkward position as several regional gold tokens — impeccable local credentials, negligible global presence. The UAE's regulatory clarity on tokenized commodities is genuinely ahead of most jurisdictions, but clarity alone doesn't create liquidity.

dgld-gold-token-sa.title: Heritage Gold, Rebooted
dgld-gold-token-sa.text: DGLD is backed by PAMP gold bars — the Swiss refiner whose name is synonymous with premium bullion — which makes its six-year disappearance and recent revival all the more puzzling. MKS PAMP relaunched DGLD in late 2025 with a Base deployment via Aerodrome, real-time reserve verification through on-chain bar serial numbers, and VQF/FINMA regulatory oversight. At somewhere between $3 million and $17 million (the data can't even agree), DGLD has the most prestigious gold backing in crypto and the least market traction. A 60-year refining heritage turns out to be necessary but wildly insufficient for winning the tokenized gold race.

kag-kinesis.title: The Lonely Ounce
kag-kinesis.text: In a world where tokenized gold has surged past $6 billion, tokenized silver remains a ghost town — and KAG is effectively its only resident. At $16 million market cap, Kinesis Silver offers the same yield-sharing model as its gold sibling KAU, but without the macro tailwind: silver was flat while gold rallied 65% in 2025. The thesis is straightforward — if precious metals tokenization is real, silver must eventually follow gold — but "eventually" is doing a lot of heavy lifting. For now, KAG is less a product and more a bet on silver's relevance in an increasingly gold-obsessed market.

eurq-quantoz.title: The Enterprise Euro
eurq-quantoz.text: Quantoz built EURQ for corporate treasurers, not DeFi degens — MiCA-compliant, DNB-regulated, 102% reserved in government bonds and Tier 1 bank deposits, with direct SEPA integration and a minimum transaction size that explicitly filters out retail. At 89 million euros in circulation it's the second-largest regulated euro stablecoin behind Circle's EURC, carving a niche in programmable corporate payments where compliance is a feature, not a tax. The 2% over-collateralization buffer is a quiet flex: enough to signal conservatism without dragging capital efficiency. Whether the enterprise market actually wants an on-chain euro or just talks about it at conferences remains the open question.

deuro-deuro.title: The Oracle-Free Euro
deuro-deuro.text: Born from the same codebase as Frankencoin (ZCHF), dEURO takes the contrarian position that price oracles are a point of failure, not a feature. Its CDP model uses internal auctions instead of external price feeds — a design that trades capital efficiency for resilience against oracle manipulation. Collateral ranges from BTC and ETH to XAUT and even USDC, making it less a purist crypto stablecoin and more an omnivorous CDP that happens to denominate in euros. With governance fully transferred to token holders and no founder control over contracts, dEURO is genuinely decentralized in a euro stablecoin market where that word usually means "we have a multisig." MiCA's evolving stance on decentralized stablecoins could be either tailwind or existential threat.

cetes-etherfuse.title: Three Counterparties, One Yield
cetes-etherfuse.text: CETES are Mexico's equivalent of Treasury bills — zero-coupon sovereign debt auctioned weekly by the Ministry of Finance — and Etherfuse has tokenized them into a NAV-accreting instrument that starts at MXN 1.00, drifts upward as the discount unwinds, and resets when each bond matures. Calling it a stablecoin is generous; the price is supposed to rise, which is what makes it useful and what disqualifies it from the description. The BBB- sovereign rating is honest about where Mexico sits in the credit hierarchy — legitimate investment grade, but peso volatility means dollar-denominated exposure carries FX risk that doesn't appear in the 5.78% APY headline. Etherfuse acts as KYC-gated intermediary between holders and INDEVAL's custody system, layering startup counterparty risk on top of sovereign risk; the third-party reserve attestation helps, though Etherfuse has not disclosed who the attesting firm is. The yield is real and Banxico's rate cycle has kept CETES competitive globally — what the token hasn't resolved is which of its three dependencies (the peso, the sovereign, or the issuer) will cause the first inconvenient conversation.

zarp-zarp.title: The Rand's Digital Outpost
zarp-zarp.text: South Africa's lone stablecoin contender holds about $3.6 million in circulation — modest by any standard, but backed by Old Mutual Wealth, one of the continent's largest financial institutions. The reserves are independently audited by Kempen, held strictly for redemption purposes, and cover the full supply at 1:1. ZARP's problem isn't credibility; it's relevance. With an FSCA CASP license still pending and South African crypto regulation in perpetual draft mode, adoption has plateaued despite deployment across Ethereum, Base, Polygon, and Solana. For a country with genuine demand for stable local-currency rails, the market has responded with a collective shrug.

syrupusdc-maple.title: Institutional Lending, Vaulted
